story:
Marquis Dortaleon died in the Sixth Roll and did not give up his seat. He had been a marquis of High Lord Baln's household, keeping the eastern road out of Baln's hall where it runs toward the Marshal's war table and the East Ward, and by the account of the demons who served under him he was a fastidious, cold, very correct peer, the kind who made sure every demon walking his road knew its line on the Roll. Then he began to rot.

The court has never said aloud what killed him, but it is not hard to guess. In the Sixth Roll the court's kitchen, under Malroch the Cook in Prince Ba'alorien's north, was working on something the Cook called a dish for the realms. Malroch needed to try it on somebody who could not complain to a prince. The Inquisitors who examined the dead marquis afterwards found a burning down his back, as if he had slept on coals, and the smell of rotten flesh in his rooms; when, many Rolls later, the court sent its Black Plague up into the three capitals, the sick in Camelot and Jordheim and Tir na Nog woke with exactly those signs. The kitchen will not confirm it. Dortaleon will not discuss it.

Grand Chancellor Adremal ruled that nothing in the bargain requires a marquis to be alive, and Dortaleon kept his line. He keeps the eastern road still, dead, correct and stinking, and Duke Harboris kept his duchy two Rolls later on the same ruling. The realms' own bestiaries list Dortaleon among the dead and not among the demons. He corrects them, when he can.
legend: Dortaleon stands on the road east out of Baln's hall, between the dukes' end of the hall and the Field Marshal's war table, which makes him easy to pull by accident during the Eligar or Nebir fights. Level 73, no script, and the world data types him undead rather than demon, which matters to anything that cares about body type. Kill him on his own before the Marshal. Players say the smell on that road is the same as the Black Plague in the capitals, and Albion players who did the plague quest swear they know it. Albion clerics joke that he is the one thing in the dungeon their prayers for the dead were written for.

loremasterTopic.text: A marquis of High Lord [Baln]'s household who died in the Sixth Roll and kept his seat, since the bargain does not require a marquis to be alive. The Inquisitors found a burning back and the smell of rot, the signs of the plague the [kitchen] later sent up into the capitals.

bookPage: From a cleric's notes, Camelot, in the season of the Black Plague: I smelled it before I saw him, on the road out of the southern hall. I knew it at once. It was the smell in the sickroom of the guard Sister Elaydith nursed, and in every room in Camelot where someone woke with their back on fire. The marquis was dead, plainly dead, and standing, and correct in every particular, and he told me to leave his road. I asked him whether the Cook had done it. He did not answer, but he looked north, toward the kitchens, for a long moment, and then he drew.
